featured_reviews.name: Aashraya Gattamraju
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are educators who teach concepts. Then there are people who quietly alter your life trajectory without even realising they did.

Dr Aman Bhonsle has been that person for me.

I first learned under him 7 years ago through Transactional Analysis at a point where I was trying to figure out where life was taking me professionally and personally. Confused. Curious. Slightly chaotic. Trying to make sense of myself and the world.

Then came Aman.
AND WHAT AN EXPERIENCE.

I genuinely don't think I have laughed till I cried in classrooms the way I have learning under him.

The man is a RIOT.

Psychologically brilliant. Ridiculously well-read. Sharp. Hilarious. Deeply human. Pop-culturally dangerous in the best way possible because somehow he'll explain a concept using something absurdly relevant and suddenly your brain decides to store it forever.

His examples live in my head RENT FREE years later.
And you don't even realise you're learning because you're too busy laughing.

Then halfway through the lecture he casually says one line that sends you into a full blown existential crisis. And that's his superpower, because you leave feeling lighter, smarter, stronger and more aware.
Like life is manageable and not so hard to face again.
Fast forward 7 years.
I'm almost 30 now. Married. A psychotherapist myself. Still learning. Still terrified by certain life chapters. Still trying to become a better human.

And somehow Aman enters this chapter too through Parenting Coaching.
Now see, some people give information.
Some people give perspective.
Very few give people confidence in themselves.
But he does so effortlessly.

owner_posts.post_text:
Spectrum Handwriting Series – Episode 2: Pencil Grasp Myths

One of the most common concerns I hear from parents and teachers is:

“My child’s handwriting is poor because they hold the pencil incorrectly.”

While pencil grasp is important, it is rarely the only factor affecting handwriting.

Effective handwriting requires a combination of several foundational skills, including:
• Hand strength and endurance
• Postural control and core stability
• Visual-motor integration
• Motor planning
• Sustained attention

Children with handwriting difficulties are often trying much harder than we realize. Repeatedly correcting their pencil grip may increase frustration without addressing the underlying challenge.

As Occupational Therapists, our focus is not only on how a child holds a pencil, but also on developing the skills that make handwriting efficient, comfortable, and meaningful.

When we build the foundation first, handwriting becomes easier and more successful.

What handwriting myths have you commonly encountered as a parent, teacher, or therapist?

✍️ Spectrum Handwriting Series | Episode 1

📝 “I keep telling him to write neatly… but his handwriting is still messy.”

This is one of the most common concerns parents share.

What many parents don’t realize is that messy handwriting is often a symptom, not the actual problem.

Handwriting is a complex skill that depends on:
✔️ Hand strength
✔️ Pencil grasp
✔️ Visual-motor skills
✔️ Motor planning
✔️ Attention
✔️ Postural control & core stability

When these foundation skills are weak, writing can become slow, tiring and frustrating—even for children who are trying their best.

Instead of asking:
❌ “Why isn’t my child trying harder?”

Let’s ask:
✅ “What is making handwriting difficult for my child?”

Early identification and the right support can make writing easier, more efficient and more enjoyable.

💚 Every child can improve when we understand the reason behind the struggle.

Many parents believe that progress happens only during therapy sessions.

But the reality is that children learn and grow through repetition, consistency, and practice in their natural environments — especially at home.

A well-designed Home Program helps children continue working on important skills between therapy sessions, including:

✅ Communication, interaction & socialisation
✅ Handwriting and fine motor skills
✅ Sensory processing
✅ School readiness
✅ Core strength and posture
✅ Feeding skills
✅ Independence in daily activities

Even 15–20 minutes of structured practice each day can make a meaningful difference.

Home programs also empower parents by giving them practical strategies to support their child’s development in everyday routines.

At Aakaar Occupational Therapy, we believe therapy is most effective when therapists and families work together as a team.

Small steps, practiced consistently, often lead to big progress.

Therapy may begin in the clinic, but meaningful progress continues at home.” 🌱

Around the world, nearly 240 million children live with disabilities—approximately 1 in every 10 children. These children may face challenges in movement, communication, learning, sensory processing, or daily self-care activities.

This is where Occupational Therapists make a meaningful difference. Through specialized interventions, they help children develop essential life skills, improve independence, enhance participation in school and social activities, and build confidence in their abilities.

Occupational Therapy is not just about treatment; it is about empowering children to reach their full potential and enabling families to create supportive environments for growth and success.

Every small achievement—a child holding a pencil, tying shoelaces, expressing emotions, or participating in classroom activities—is a step toward a more inclusive world.

Every milestone matters. When a child learns a new skill, gains confidence, or participates more fully in everyday life, it reflects the power of timely support and intervention. Occupational Therapists play a vital role in helping children overcome barriers, discover their strengths, and engage meaningfully in the activities that matter most to them. Together, we can create a world where every child has the opportunity to thrive, participate, and succeed.
